stem: One source batch is divided across two dry-room racks. What is required for traceability?
choices: Link the source batch only to the first rack because the second rack shares the same harvest event.
Keep both receiving rack or lot identities linked to the same source transformation, including required quantity and event data for each split.
Close the source identity once the batch is divided because the new rack IDs become authoritative.
Use one combined unlabeled record for both racks so the split does not create duplicate records.
rationale: When one source batch is split, both outputs must remain traceable to the original source and transformation event. Each receiving identity/location needs enough quantity and event context to reconstruct the split. Deleting the source relationship or collapsing both outputs into one unlabeled record breaks genealogy.
